intent: The grid that lays out a QuestionnaireItem's choices, and its freeform field when the item offers one beside them.
typical_uses: The list of fixed answers of an item
Fixed answers followed by a freeform "other" field

dont_use_when.situation: An item whose only answer is freeform text

instead.target: QuestionnaireInput placed directly in the QuestionnaireItem

invariants.text: When the root has `shortcuts`, the grid carries `data-shortcuts` with the mode (`letters` or `numbers`).

anti_patterns.dont: Place a freeform QuestionnaireInput outside QuestionnaireChoices in an item that also has choices
anti_patterns.do_instead: Make it the last child of QuestionnaireChoices, so it sits on the choice grid's rhythm

render.states: render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies
render.because: The questionnaire engine's render prop takes an element or a function of the grid's own state (`QuestionnaireChoicesState`: shortcuts), so its type is a union of a React element and a callback; the compiler emits one JSON type per property, so nothing is asserted.

good.title: Fixed choices and a freeform field
good.code:
<QuestionnaireChoices>
  <QuestionnaireChoice value="tool-calls">Tool call timeline</QuestionnaireChoice>
  <QuestionnaireChoice value="approvals">Approval checkpoints</QuestionnaireChoice>
  <QuestionnaireInput aria-label="Another feature" placeholder="Describe another feature" />
</QuestionnaireChoices>

bad.title: Choices wrapped in a RadioGroup
bad.why: The item already groups its choices as native radios sharing its name; a RadioGroup adds a second selection state that the questionnaire never reads.

render.description: TS: RenderProp<QuestionnaireChoicesState> | undefined. The compiler emits one JSON type per property; this type is left to tsc. render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies. The questionnaire engine's render prop takes an element or a function of the grid's own state (`QuestionnaireChoicesState`: shortcuts), so its type is a union of a React element and a callback; the compiler emits one JSON type per property, so nothing is asserted.
